introduction.p: Plot a graph for the equation y=\frac{4}{3}x-4\text{.}

statement.p: First, make a table. This equation doesnt have any context to help us choose x-values for a table. We could use x-values like -2\text{,} -1\text{,} and so on. But take note that there is a fraction in the equation. If we are clever, we can avoid fraction arithmetic which is a source of human error. If we use only multiples of 3 for the x-values, then multiplying by \frac{4}{3} will leave us with an integer. So we decide to use -6\text{,} -3\text{,} 0\text{,} 3\text{,} and 6 for x\text{.}
Use points from the table to graph the equation.

sidebyside.p: First, plot each point carefully. Then connect the points with a smooth line/curve. Here, the curve is a straight line.
